text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Former Polish president Lech Walesa has announced plans to form a political party following parliamentary elections in September.
The new party will not be formed prior to the elections so as not to spoil the opportunities of existing political forces, Walesa said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Kredyt Bank's board will propose its general shareholders meeting to issue shares worth more than 200 million zlotys to obtain funds needed to acquire Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and Prosper Bank.

The cabinet's recent decision for National Investment Funds (NFIs) to pay a 36 percent tax from January 1998 on profits from sales of their firms appears wrong in both the short and long term, Gdansk Institute for Market Economy president Jan Szomburg said.
- Sales of the plant of vegetable and fruit processing firm Hortex in the southern town of Lezajsk reached 100 million zlotys in the 1995/1996 season.
Sales in the 1996/1997 season will rise to 110 million zlotys, the company said.

- The Chemix-Truck paint and lacquer distribution firm has started assembly of Belarus-made MAZ trucks in a newly opened assembly plant in Debnica Kaszubska, northern Poland. Chemix plans to open 12 dealer branches around the country and a similar number of service points.
- Petrus life insurance firm is mulling a new share issue worth 20 million zlotys to increase the firm's share capital from the current 4.5 million zlotys.

- France's Credit Lyonnais, which holds a 27 percent stake in IBP Bank in Warsaw, is planning to buy the remaining shares in the bank and to change it into a fully owned subsidiary, a source who declined to be named said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Halex Shipping Company of Elblag, which transports imported Russian coal from the Kaliningrad district to Poland, has offered to buy a controlling stake in the municipal power and heating plant in Braniewo, northern Poland.
- Polish-U.S. trade exchange rose to $2.187 billion last year from $1.351 billion in 1993.
Poland's trade deficit from the exchange is at $1.096 billion.

- The Macrosoft computer system integrator has presented an information memorandum to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) concerning Macrosoft's listing on the over-the-counter (CTO) market planned for this summer, the firm's marketing director Pawel Bondar said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The listed Lodzka Drukarnia Akcydensowa (LDA) printing plant's board is planning to spend last year's net profit of 831,300 zlotys on investment to increase production, a source who declined to be named said.
ZYCIE
- A number of Poland's pasta makers are responsible for a significant quality decline.
They do not add the required amount of eggs and semolina flour and subsitute them with excessive amounts of food colouring, a report by the PIH state trading standards authority said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
